gaps.quote: It is the endpoint operator of the bit procedure
gaps.note: The page never says what the bit procedure is, what the construction it versions is, or what an endpoint of it is. It gives only 'the version of the construction that works on single bits through XOR gates' and does not link a wiki page for it. The later phrase 'the linear network of the bit procedure, at its endpoint' depends on the same unexplained term.

gaps.quote: it is one of the linear-cost address updates that interchange two address fields
gaps.note: The page claims the shear is a linear-cost update, but the only cost it states is for the two outer updates. It never says what the network's middle shear costs, so the reader cannot check that the shear itself is linear-cost.

gaps.term: how the network performs the shear
gaps.quote: The network performs it by splitting rows into role streams, applying its gates pointwise at matching addresses, and merging the rows back.
gaps.note: The reader knows role streams and pointwise gates by name, but the page does not say what the gates compute at matching addresses or why splitting, gating and merging yields (H,D) mapped to (H+D,D). The claim that the network performs the shear cannot be checked from the page.

gaps.quote: they cost linear time per unit volume
gaps.note: The cited claim's content is not fully stated: 'volume' is never defined, so the reader cannot tell what size measure the linear bound is taken against.
